text:
sasha: :rotating_light: infra alert — sudden throughput drop on ded-gpu-pool in us-west-2, Datadog showing burst of NVLINK frame errors + AER XID 31 on rack19. Noting elevated tail latency for gen2 workloads.
infra-bot: [ALERT] nvlink_errors > 50/min (rack19) — triggered at 2026-03-12T03:14:22Z — compare: baseline 0.3/min.
datadog: (automated) linked graph: nvlink_frame_errors / gpu_utilization / pod_p95_latency — spike around 03:12 UTC.
mike: looking at the node logs now, getting repeated AER messages and link re-negotiation:```kernel: pcie0: AER: Multiple Corrected error, dev 0000:3b:00.0, status=0x1e, severity=corrected
kernel: nvlink: link 2: LINK_FLAP detected
kernel: nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: Xid (31) 00000000
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors,utilization.gpu --format=csv
GPU 0, CE=12, UE=0, Util=65%```
olivia: which pods are on the affected nodes? are these training jobs or latency-critical endpoints?
mike: mostly batch/embedding jobs on dedicated pool but a few small prod reranker replicas on the same pool (mis-scheduled). I'll paste node list: rack19-node03, rack19-node05, rack19-node08 show repeats.
raj: plan proposal — immediate steps: 1) cordon affected nodes (one at a time), 2) drain non-prod workloads and reschedule to ded-gpu-pool-2, 3) mark GPUs as degraded and RMA suspect cards (probably nvlink PHY or riser), 4) open vendor case and attach nvlink dumps + kernel traces. Recommend 2-node rolling to keep throughput.
sasha: agree with rolling 2 nodes. also enable nvlink link-state logging at debug level and capture nvlink_error counters for 6 hours before hardware swap.
mike: running commands now:```kubectl cordon rack19-node05
kubectl drain rack19-node05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=30m
ssh rack19-node05 'sudo nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PCI,POWER
sudo journalctl -k | tail -n 200 | grep -i nvlink'```
infra-bot: drain started for rack19-node05 by mike at 2026-03-12T03:23:45Z.
olivia: creating incident ticket INFRA-3421 and vendor case NVL-7789, assigning to hw-ops. Adding notebook with nvlink dumps and nvidia-smi captures.
raj: RMA scope: replace suspect GPUs on node05 and node08. If errors persist after swap, escalate to backplane/riser inspection.
mike: quick sanity: we see ECC CE counts jumping but UEs remain 0. Xid 31 is page table fault caused by link resets. Suspect noisy NVLink lane.
sasha: note to SRE: route latency-critical rerank replicas off ded-gpu-pool until we confirm stability. Put a soft quota to avoid accidental scheduling back.
olivia: tagging on-call infra rotation: @mike @raj please update within 30m with post-drain status.
mike: update — node05 drained, jobs rescheduled, nvlink errors persisted during drain but decreased after taking node out of service. Collecting nvlink_dump and full dmesg now.
raj: if stable for 1 hour after removing two nodes, we can proceed to scheduled RMA window tomorrow 02:00 UTC. If flaps continue after cards swapped, we'll open a follow-up for riser/backplane and consider rack power sequencing.
sasha: thanks team. keeping this thread as the single place for updates. I'll annotate the runbook with commands used and link INFRA-3421.
datadog: suppression rule applied to avoid noisy alerts for nodal drains; monitor remaining racks.
mike: attaching nvidia-smi snapshot & nvlink_dump to ticket (links in INFRA-3421). Will kick off vendor case.
raj: executing hardware ticket now. vendor case NVL-7789 created with priority P2. expected hold for RMA parts: 3-5 business days.
sasha: final note — consider steering batch workloads to us-east-1 for next 48h to reduce risk during RMA. :thumbsup:
